newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher in lower volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged higher in selective and quiet trade on Friday after the market was a bit disappointed with the results of a late Thursday meeting of the Higher Board of Privatisation (OYK), brokers said.

"Activity died down and trade margins narrowed, but there wasn't any pessimism. The approval of only a few sell offs at yesterday's privatisation meeting depressed activity," said Berra Kilic from Ata securities.
The IMKB National-100 closed five points, or 0.3 percent firmer at 1,654, bringing weekly gains to 10.34 percent after last week's 3.88 percent rise.
Trade volume shrank to 32.93 trillion lira ($261.1 million) from 45.48 trillion ($363.1 million) on Thursday.

The privatisation of three banks, a cement firm, a tyre maker and a maritime cargo company for $600 million were passed by the OYK, out of an expected 20 with a total best bid value of $881.7 million.
Privatisation hopes had enlivened ahead of the Board meeting, buoying demand in state-controlled firms.
"Selective activity may continue in light of first quarter profit prospects from now on because the release of all 1996 financial reports (this week) ended expectations," Kilic said.
